summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of liver transplant, colorectal cancer, and chronic malnutrition, was admitted from rehab due to hypoxia and failed feeding tube replacement. He developed hospital-acquired pneumonia with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, confirmed by bronchoalveolar lavage, and was electively intubated for NJ tube placement. After successful bronchoscopy with mucus plug removal and tube placement, he was extubated and transitioned to room air. Tube feeds were restarted post-pylorically to reduce aspiration risk, and IV antibiotics were continued for a 14-day course. His infection resolved, nutritional support was established, and he was discharged to extended care with plans to complete antibiotics and follow up with hepatology and psychiatry.
